Incident Involving Mayuree Naree

Precious Shipping PCL 3
Incident Involving Mayuree Naree  in the Strait of Hormuz
•The vessel was most likely struck by two projectiles in the engine room , causing a fire while 
transiting the Strait of Hormuz at approximately 08:15 hours LT on 11th March 2026 .
•20 Thai crew members  were safely evacuated and arrived  in Thailand on 16th March while 
three Thai crew members remained missing . 
•Prior to and during the transit, the Vessel implemented enhanced security precautions and 
maintained communication with the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) 
and other relevant maritime security coordination centers, while providing regular position 
reports  in accordance with applicable advisories .
•The Vessel was instructed  to follow  the latest advisories issued by the UKMTO and other 
relevant maritime security authorities . The Vessel did not receive any specific warnings 
from any authority while underway on her passage. 
•On 22nd March , the Mayuree Naree  reportedly ran aground off Qeshm  Island, Iran .

Precious Shipping PCL 4
Incident Involving Mayuree Naree  in the Strait of Hormuz
•On 30th March , after the receipt of the necessary permissions from the relevant local Iranian authorities, 
a specialist search team boarded the vessel to conduct a search operation in the areas where the three 
missing crew members were last believed to be located . The search was carried out under challenging 
conditions , including the presence of fire damage , residual smoke , and flooding in the engine room , 
and all accessible areas were examined to the extent possible . Despite these efforts, the search team 
was unable  to locate any of the three missing crew members. 
•Second and third onboard searches were conducted on 1 April and 7 April , respectively, following which 
the remains of the three crew members were located.
•At this stage, further forensic investigations and the repatriation of the remains and bodies are being 
pursued  in coordination with the relevant Iranian authorities and the Royal Thai Embassy in Iran. Families 
of the crew have been informed  of this development. The Company reaffirms its full commitment to 
supporting the families during this difficult time.
•On 16th April , the war risk underwriters paid an amount of USD 10.9m to the Company , primarily in 
respect of the constructive total loss of the vessel and compensation for the crew and their families.
•From an accounting perspective, USD 10.9 million insurance proceeds were recorded as an insurance 
receivable in 1Q26 pending receipt in April 2026. The recovery was already netted against the related 
vessel incident loss in the P&L (resulting in no net loss for the insured portion ), with only compensation 
paid in excess of insurance coverage recognized as an expense.

Precious Shipping PCL 5
The impact of the current war between USA -Israel versus Iran

Precious Shipping PCL 6
Dry Bulk – Major disruption to key markets 
•~4% of global dry -bulk demand normally transits the Strait of Hormuz 
•West Asia is a critical global supply hub for key dry -bulk inputs: 
•Fertilisers: ~25 –30% of global seaborne fertiliser trade originates from West Asia, including 
~31% of global urea exports
•Sulphur: ~40 –45% of global seaborne sulphur exports originate from West Asia
•Gypsum: ~20 –25% of global seaborne gypsum trade originates from the region, 
•These cargoes are almost entirely export -oriented and highly dependent on Hormuz, with 
limited short -term alternative routing
•Following escalation, fertiliser, sulphur, limestone, gypsum shipments through Hormuz 
collapsed by ~90%+  month -on-month, reflecting both physical disruption and risk aversion
•~2% of global dry -bulk fleet capacity temporarily removed , as vessels were stranded, idling, 
diverting, or avoiding the Gulf altogether
•Offsetting factor: sustained high gas and LNG prices may boost coal demand , particularly 
Australian high -CV coal, benefiting Panamax/Supramax segments if disruption persists
•Asian buyers of Fertilisers, Sulphur, Gypsum will need to procure these commodities from the 
Western Hemisphere, boosting dry -bulk tonne mile

Precious Shipping PCL 7
Product Tankers (MR / CPP) – Clear short -term beneficiaries
•West Asia is structurally critical to clean product supply : 
•~12% of global refined product trade  originates from West Asia
•West Asia accounts for ~15 –20% of global diesel, jet fuel, and naphtha exports , 
supplying Europe, Africa, and parts of Asia
•Disruption to Hormuz and Red Sea routes has forced major re -routing of West Asian product 
exports, driving significant tonne -mile inflation 
•Stoppage of West Asia crude exports forces Asian and European refiners to replace West Asian 
barrels with longer -haul Atlantic Basin and other alternative crudes, disrupting refinery runs 
and changing crude sourcing economics.
•As these crude -importing hubs lose feedstock , refinery throughput is reduced and surplus 
product exports from Asia and Europe disappear. The loss of these refinery -linked product 
exports reshapes global clean product trade flows, pushing importing regions to source 
products from farther afield. This re -routing supports product tanker tonne -miles even as 
overall clean product volumes soften
•Result: MR and clean tanker earnings surged, with Atlantic MRs returning to USD 
~80k/day+ at present

Precious Shipping PCL 12
Iron ore imports rise even as China’s steel sector cools
▪China’s iron ore imports hit a record 314.8 MMT in Q1 2026 (+10.3% YoY), accounting for  the 
majority of global import demand growth.
▪Steel exports declined ~10% YoY , with Q1 2026 marking the weakest quarter since 2023 amid new 
export licensing . 
▪Reduced Middle East Gulf steel exports have opened Southeast Asia opportunities for China and 
India.
▪China’s iron ore port stockpiles have reached record highs .
▪Australia  drove the bulk of China’s iron ore import growth (~+15 MMT YoY) , rebounding from cyclone -
disrupted 2025 levels, while Brazil  added further ~5 MMT with nearly 3x higher tonne -mile demand .
▪Emerging supply diversification, with first shipments from Guinea reaching China, alongside record 
volumes from Liberia and stronger flows from Venezuela . All longer tonne -mile.
Source: Braemar as of 23 Apr 2026 

Precious Shipping PCL 13
Dry Bulk Trade and Tariff Impacts in 2025, if any
▪China exported 209.3  MMT , 3.8% of global dry bulk exports  mainly to  East Asia/South -East Asia 
and Latin America . The US accounted for just 1.8% of China’s dry bulk exports , or 3.68 MMT in 
2025.
▪In 2025, China imported 2,190.5 MMT (41%) of global dry bulk imports , EU 8.1%, India 6.7%. In 
2024, China imported 2,275.9 MMT (41%) of global dry bulk imports , EU 7.9%, India 6.8%.
▪In 2025, China imported 1,229.5 MMT of iron ore, 379.7 MMT of coal, 192.1 MMT of bauxite, 99.6 
MMT of agri -bulks, 45.3 MMT of nickel ore, 27.2 MMT of grains, 36.7 MMT of forest products, 28.9 
MMT of woodchips, and 26.5 MMT of manganese.
▪US exported just 1.1% of dry bulk goods to China, or 2 4.54 MMT ( -53.2% y -o-y) in 2025, showing 
an unofficial boycott of US from China (6.5 MMT of soybeans, 1.8 MMT of grains, 4.5 MMT of coal, 
and 0.8 MMT of fertilizers). All fungible cargoes.
▪It is obvious that any tariff war can ONLY hurt the US and certainly not China in the dry bulk 
space .
Source: Banchero Costa Research

Precious Shipping PCL 22
MR Tanker - Tharinee  Naree
▪We signed  an MOA  to acquire  one MR Tanker  – Tharinee  Naree , (47,999 DWT,  built 2006), 
from Asia Pacific  Shipping  Co., Ltd. Delivered  to PSL on 26th February  2026 . 
▪Purchase  price  of USD  11.10 million . 
▪Total  cost of 4th Special  Survey  is estimated  at $2.2m.
▪The first voyage  made  by the Tharin ee Naree  has realised  about  $25,000 per day, with the 
second  voyage  expected  to achieve  between  $33,000-$42,000 per day.
▪Marks  our entry  into the lucrative  oil segment,  reducing  reliance  on dry-bulk and establishing  a 
dual-sector  revenue  stream .
▪A critical  steppingstone  for future  expansion  into larger  Tanker  segments  and the Gas carrier  
market .

Precious Shipping PCL 23
Introduction to the MR Tanker Segment
•The MR (Medium Range ~25,000 -55,000 dwt) tanker segment primarily transports refined 
petroleum products (on short to medium -haul routes) such as:
➢Gasoline
➢Diesel / gasoil
➢Jet fuel
➢Naphtha
Why it matters?
•MR tankers transport finished fuels from refineries to consuming markets
•They are the main vessel type used for regional and inter -regional clean product trade
•Demand is strongly influenced by:
➢Differences in fuel supply and demand between neighbouring regions
➢Temporary/permanent refinery shutdowns and maintenance
➢Seasonal changes in fuel consumption (summer vs winter)
➢Sanctioned tankers/Shadow fleet
➢Disruption in the Red Sea, Black Sea and the Persian Gulf
